newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent bounces off lows, good fund WTI buying.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent bounces off lows, good fund WTI buying.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil bounced off the lows on Tuesday on the back of good fund buying which focused mainly on NYMEX crude, brokers said. Prompt contracts then dipped back down as locals sold into the market.
June Brent traded at 1455 GMT down nine cents at $19.63 a barrel, off the days low of $19.56 a barrel. The contract had traded up to a high of $19.78 earlier.

"The markets were looking for a correction after yesterday's gains. The feeling was that Monday's rally was overdone, but we have seen consistently good buying from Wall Street and London (IPE) has given up trying to go down," one broker said.
"There is some low volume selling coming in on the prompt contract, but the July is holding strong," another said.
The July contract was most actively traded with over 10,000 lots done and the contract last move steady at $19.47 a barrel.
The June gas oil contract was last done up 25 cents at $174 a tonne.
Prompt Brent jumped nearly 80 cents on Monday.

Some brokers were still cautious of the recent gains and said that volumes were not high enough for Monday's move to hold without a downward correction. "I'm not convinced about the move yet. We need to see more fund buying," one commented.
On the upside the prompt June contract saw a gap at $19.90-92 which was the next point of resistance. Support at $19.50 was strong, brokers said.
